exposure: known vs. unknown cause of RPL
cohort: 323 women with two or more pregnancy losses without any live birth in a tertiary care institute in South India
finding: In women with recurrent pregnancy loss, thrombophilias were the most common cause, and while there was no difference in miscarriage or live birth rates between known and unknown RPL,  IUGR, stillbirth, and perinatal deaths were higher in known RPL after interventions; in unknown RPL, thromboprophylaxis with aspirin alone resulted in higher preterm birth, while combined therapy with enoxaparin and/or progesterone resulted in higher term birth rates.
